name: Mehrabad International Airport
before:
Iran's busiest airport by passengers and aircraft movements, in Tehran, though the name can mislead. Since Imam Khomeini International opened in 2007 and took the international flights, Mehrabad has handled mostly domestic traffic. A client flying into Tehran from abroad will almost certainly not land here.

It carried 17,464,216 passengers in 2017 and serves 60 non-stop destinations through 23 airlines, with Iran Air the largest operator.

There are four active terminals and the airline allocation matters. Terminal 2, from 1977, is the busiest and handles Iran Air among others. Terminal 4, from 2007, takes Caspian, Iran Aseman and FlyPersia.

Terminal 1 is worth a look. Opened in 1955, it was the first advanced airport terminal in the Middle East and is now registered as a national historical monument in Iran, both for its architecture and for its place in the country's development.

The airport opened in 1938 and is also used by the Iranian government and air force.
after:
Tehran's domestic airport, in the west of the city. International flights use Imam Khomeini instead.

Iran closed its airspace after the United States and Israel struck the country on 28 February 2026. Mehrabad reopened in mid-April, but Iranian airspace can still close at short notice, and European regulators tell their airlines not to fly in it at any altitude.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran, and the US government tells its citizens not to travel there for any reason.
